IncidentBot: PAGER: multiple serving nodes in us-west-2 reporting repeated container restarts, high tail latency, and CUDA OOMs. Auto-escalation to on-call SRE. Start investigating: nodes in rack r12-r15.
Ashley (oncall): acked. I'm on it. seeing a burst of `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` in serve-runtime logs plus `rdma: retransmit` events in ethtool stats.
MattB: can you paste the container logs / dmesg? suspect RDMA packet loss triggering NCCL retries and kv cache thrash.
Ashley (oncall): paste logs below:
```
[2026-03-15T02:10:21Z] serve-runtime: worker-3: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY while allocating 512MB kv-cache
[2026-03-15T02:10:21Z] nccl: ERROR plugin: AllReduce failed, ret=2
[2026-03-15T02:10:22Z] kernel: mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: HW error: link recovery
[2026-03-15T02:10:24Z] rdma: qp 0x7f: retransmit timeout (pkt loss)
```
Sana: adding infra-eng. This looks like intra-rack IB fabric flaps. Could be a switch microburst or driver mismatch.
Kevin: are the drivers recently rolled? any change window?
Infra-ENG: rollouts: no driver rollouts in last 48h. We saw a partial power maintenance 3h ago on rack PDU but nothing noted flagged.
Ashley (oncall): I ran `ibstat` on node node-r12-{02,03,04}: port state alternates between Active and Fatal. Running `mlnx_diag` shows TX drops on port 1.
MattB: try toggling `rdma-net-probe` frequency and enable link-layer retries? quick mitigation: mark affected nodes `unschedulable` in the serving pool and route traffic to healthy nodes.
Ashley (oncall): draining nodes now with: `kubectl cordon node-r12-02 && k scale --replicas=0 deploy/serve-node-group-r12` — starting traffic shift.
IncidentBot: NOTE: Automated fallback policy engaged for customers pinned to RDMA-backed pools -> routing to CPU/PCIe fallback models for latency-sensitive routes.
Support-Lead: quick customer impact: dashboards show 500 errors spike from 0.4% -> 8.7% for customers on dedicated-usw2-rdma. Tail latency (p99) jumped from 120ms -> 1.2s. Affected customers: 3 Dedicated tenants, 1 Hosted tenant on routed jobs.
Customer-SRE: pinging account owners for the three dedicated customers, preparing incident banner.
Sana: are we seeing container crashes due to OOM only, or also driver resets?
Ashley (oncall): both. dmesg shows `mlx5_core fw reset` followed by multiple `nv_peer_mem` detach/attach and then the CUDA OOMs as kernels restart. Pattern: link flap -> nccl fallback -> KV cache thrash -> OOMs while re-warming caches.
Kevin: immediate ask: can we throttle the warmup batch size or disable aggressive KV prefetch on affected nodes? That'll reduce memory pressure during unstable network conditions.
MattB: yes, set env var `KV_PREFETCH=false` in serve-runtime config for the affected node pool and deploy via `kubectl set env`. This should reduce cold-start allocations.
Infra-ENG: creating a fabric probe job: `for n in node-r12-{02..15}; do ssh $n "ibv_devinfo && ethtool -S mlx5_core"; done` — collecting counters.
IncidentBot: PagerDuty: escalation to senior network + runtime engineers after 15m if no resolution.
Ashley (oncall): mitigation steps executed: nodes cordoned + KV_PREFETCH disabled on pool, fallback routing enabled, new requests draining off RDMA nodes. Observed error rate dropping to 3.2% after 7 minutes.
Sana: good. still seeing intermittent link resets on r12-07. are spare links available to re-patch?
Infra-ENG: ops: rack-level redundancy limited, but we can move critical pods to adjacent rack r10 which still has spare capacity. Planning live pod migration.
Support-Lead: drafting customer comms: short note explaining transient RDMA fabric issues causing increased errors and latency, mention mitigations and ETA for update in 30m.
Kevin: for longer term: suggest adding proactive RDMA link-level healthchecks to console (alerts when retransmit count > threshold), and a runtime knob to auto-slow-warm caches under network instability. File an RFC?
MattB: capturing the trace: `serve-runtime` trace IDs: trc-usr-9a7f02.. attached to this thread. We should attach to postmortem.
Ashley (oncall): handing off to MattB for night coverage. I'm flagging the incident as active and will update handoff notes. Current state: 6 nodes drained, 9 remaining RDMA nodes in pool; fallback routing covers ~65% of traffic for affected customers; error rate stable ~2.8%.
MattB: taking over. next actions: continue fabric diagnostics, schedule spare-link swap for r12-07, coordinate with on-site tech to inspect SFP/QSFP on node pairs. I'll update in 20m or earlier.
IncidentBot: oncall-handoff: previous_oncall=Ashley (oncall); new_oncall=MattB; handoff_ts=1987654720.
Customer-SRE: sent initial notice to affected tenants, set follow-up for 60m.
Support-Lead: timeline note: incident created 1987654321; mitigation partial at +7m; routing fallback engaged +10m; handoff +8m; next update in 20m.
Ashley (oncall): adding quick blameless note: fabric appears to be the root cause, network-induced retries amplified runtime memory pressure -> container restarts. Will capture metrics for KB: `rdma.retransmit.count`, `serve.kv.prefetch.allocs`, `cuda.oom.count`.
MattB: acknowledged. tagging this thread for postmortem.
IncidentBot: If next escalation threshold hit, PD will page `senior-net` and `sre-leads` in 10m. Keep comms in this thread. :thumbsup:
